content.title: St. John's vs. Duke score, highlights as Johnnies fall short in Sweet 16
content.text: March 27, 2026Updated March 28, 2026, 12:13 a.m. ETSt. John’s historic run in the NCAA Tournament has come to an end. The Johnnies came up short in a 80-75 loss to Duke in the Sweet 16 on Friday night. Despite holding a double digit lead in the second half, the Blue Devils were too much to overcome for the Red Storm, who were making their first Sweet 16 appearance since 1999. St. John's guard Dylan Darling, who had the game-winning shot against Kansas in the Round of 32, missed a game-tying three-pointer in the final seconds of the game.Duke was led by guard Isaiah Evans, who had a game-high 25 points and freshman sensation forward Cameron Boozer, a projected top pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, who finished with 22 points and 10 rebounds.Duke, the top overall seed in the NCAA Tournament, now awaits the winner of UConn and Michigan State in the Elite Eight on Sunday. Here was our live coverage and analysis of the thrilling St. John’s vs. Duke Sweet 16 matchup in the East Regional semifinal of the NCAA Tournament: Sweet 16 final score: Duke 80, St. John's 75It's officially struck midnight for St. John's.The Johnnies have been eliminated from the NCAA Tournament after a 80-75 loss against Duke in the Sweet 16.St. John's gave the the No. 1 overall seed Blue Devils their toughest test yet, as the Red Storm held the advantage at halftime and were up by as many as 10 points in the second half.It still wasn't enough, as Duke continuously dominated the Red Storm and finally started to hit shots from the outside.Despite the loss, what a run it's been for St. John's.From 2000-2022, the Johnnies had one win in the NCAA Tournament.The Red Storm had two victories alone in this year's March Madness and three tournament wins in three years under head coach Rick Pitino, who has completely turned this program around in short order.In that span under Pitino, St. John's has averaged 27 wins a season with a .771 winning percentage and won back-to-back Big East regular season titles and consecutive conference championships under the Hall-of-Fame head coach.The loss may sting now for St. John's, but you know with Pitino at the helm they'll be right back in contention next season to build off of the most successful season in the last quarter century for the Red Storm. Duke holds huge free-throw advantage over St. John'sA key difference in the game is the free-throw differential for Duke.With less than five minutes left in regulation, the Blue Devils own 18-6 advantage over St. John's at the line.A large reason for this is that St. John's has been unable to establish any type of consistency in the post or paint throughout this game. St. John's opens up largest lead of Sweet 16 game over DukeThe Johnnies couldn't have asked for a better start coming out of the break.St. John's is up 55-45 just past the five-minute mark of the second half, currently on a 15-1 run.A large part of that has been Ruben Prey, who is perfect from the field with 12 points, as he's 4-of-4 from behind the arc and had a huge block after drilling a three-pointer.The Red Storm have made their last seven shots while they've forced five consecutive misses from Duke. St. John's, Duke going back-and-forth in second half of Sweet 16It's a heavyweight fight in D.C.It's a tie game between St. John's and Duke near the six-minute mark.St. John's and Duke have traded blows, as the Blue Devils has erased the Johnnies double digit lead.Shots are starting to fall from the outside for Duke, something that didn't happen frequently in the first half.While St. John's is still hitting shots from three-point range, the Red Storm have yet to establish a paint presence, as they're getting outscored 36-22 in points in the paint and outrebounded 33-20 by Duke.Troubling trends for the Johnnies if they can't narrow the margins in those categories. St. John's starts second half strong against DukeThe Red Storm continue where they left off in the first half.St. John's has gone on a 10-0 run in 90 seconds in the opening minutes of the second half. End of first half: St. John's 40, Duke 39What a finish to the first half for St. John's.The Red Storm enter the break with a one-point lead over the Blue Devils, ending the half on a 12-4.The Johnnies held Duke without a basket for nearly the last five minutes.Three-point range has been the key factor for St. John's, as they've already converted on nine three-pointers in the first 20 minutes of play.This includes clutch back-to-back three-pointers in the final minute from sophomore Ruben Prey, who only had 13 points over the course of the first two games of the NCAA Tournament.The difference for the Blue Devils has been in the paint, where Duke has outscored St. John's 22-10 inside. Zuby Ejiofor, the Big East conference's Player of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year, has not had a huge impact in the game so far, as he's been unable to have sustained success inside against Cameron Boozer and the Blue Devils defense. St. John's trims Duke lead to two in finale minute of first halfThe Red Storm aren't done yet.Despite being outscored 22-14 since the nine-minutes remaining in the first half, St. John's is within a basket after a corner three-pointer from Ruben Prey.The long ball is keeping the Johnnies in this one, as they're shooting 47 percent (8-of-17) from three-point range. Duke's paint presence the difference so far against St. John'sThe Blue Devils dominance down low is starting to pay off.Duke owns a 35-28 lead nearing the three-minute mark of the first half.St. John's has struggled over the last five minutes, as the Blue Devils have outscored the Red Storm 17-5 over last five minutes.Rick Pitino's squad needs an answer and quick before intermission. St. John's, Duke trade baskets in high-flying first halfDuke has responded after St. John's jumped out to their biggest lead of the game.The Blue Devils are thriving near the basket, as they're outscoring the Red Storm 18-8 in the paint.St. John's has a three-point lead with under eight minutes left in the first half.A fun one is brewing in the nation's capital. St. John's rallies, holds two-point advantage at seven-minute markAfter struggling early, St. John's has taken their first lead of the game on a three-pointer from Ian Jackson.The Johnnies are on a 12-2 run over the last two minutes heading into the second TV timeout.Great response from the Red Storm. Duke holds slim lead over St. John's early in first halfWhat a start in D.C.St. John's found themselves in a unusual position, as they were down by as many as seven points in the opening minutes of this Sweet 16 game.Coming into the Sweet 16, the Johnnies trailed only 38 seconds in the entire NCAA Tournament.The Red Storm did respond prior to the first TV timeout as a Dillon Mitchell stole the inbounds under the basket and put it home to cut into the Blue Devils lead. Our predictionSt. John's were clear betting favorites in their first two matchups against Northern Iowa and Kansas.The same can not be said here, as they're 6.5-point underdogs against Duke, who is one of the top-three odds-on-favorite to win it all.I'm calling for the upset here, as Rick Pitino continues to show why he's one of the best coaches of all time and leads the Red Storm to the massive upset and an Elite Eight appearance for St. John's for the first time in over four decades with a narrow victory over Duke.Prediction: St. John's 78, Duke 74
